Date

results.title: The fastest, lowest-cost batch transcription with Qwen3-ASR
results.author: Hasan Khan, Ansel Erol
highlights:
Hasan Khan

Ansel Erol

Published

November 2, 2026

...

We optimized Qwen3-ASR 1.7B on Baseten to achieve the lowest cost per audio minute across all transcription providers. Compared with out-of-the-box vLLM, the optimized stack transcribes 7x more audio per second at high concurrency.

...

### Cost per audio hour

Throughput affects the price, since you can get more done with the same GPU minute (or second). 

At Baseten's list price for a dedicated RTX PRO 6000 and the sustained throughput listed above, the optimized deployment transcribes an hour of audio for about 1/10th of a cent ($0.0013 per audio hour), 8x lower than the same model on vanilla vLLM at $0.011. 

Our implementation also costs around 277x less than popular closed-weight providers, which range between $0.21-$0.36. 

Baseten cost is estimated by saturating one RTX PRO 6000 on hour-long files and using list pricing; closed provider pricing is estimated from published pay-as-you-go pricing for their current flagship batch models as of the last update date of this blog.

results.title: Serverless Loops
highlights:
Serverless Loops

# Serverless Loops

Date

November 6, 2026

Serverless Loops is now generally available. You can post-train a model with supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning without reserving GPUs, and pay only for the tokens you train and sample.

Serverless Loops supports models like Qwen3.6 35B A3B, GLM 5.3, and GLM 5.3 Flash, each at sequence lengths up to 262,144 tokens.

For other models, or to control throughput with your own trainer and sampler replicas, use dedicated Loops. When training finishes, deploy the checkpoint to Baseten inference.

results.title: The platform for inference, training, and execution | Baseten
results.author: Kimbrian Canavan, Raymond Cano, Ardin Lo
highlights:
November 6, 2026

Today, Serverless Loops is generally available. Loops is a training SDK for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) on frontier open models, with a direct path to production. Train through a familiar Tinker-compatible API, evaluate your checkpoints, and deploy the resulting model to Baseten Dedicated Inference.

With the API, you focus on the training signal rather than worrying about all the finicky details of building and operating a robust, large-scale training backend. We take care of the GPUs, the kernels, the model architectures, as well as the performance and numerical correctness of the distributed training infrastructure.

As part of our initial launch, you will have access to a selection of popular open-weight models for post-training at a 256k context length for both SFT and RL. We have a competitive per-token billing model (see full details below), so you only pay for what you use.

...

If you prefer dedicated throughput, request dedicated capacity. If you’re bringing your own training stack, explore Baseten Training Jobs for managed GPU infrastructure or RL Rollouts for scalable rollouts with your own trainer.

results.title: Mixed-mode rolling promotions
highlights:
Mixed-mode rolling promotions

# Mixed-mode rolling promotions

Date

November 1, 2026

Rolling promotions now let you set max surge and max unavailable together. Control how many extra replicas Baseten can provision and how much serving capacity can temporarily decrease during the same rollout. This gives you more flexibility when spare GPU capacity is limited.

Configure both limits in your environment’s Promotion settings, through the Management API using:

```bash
curl --request PATCH \
  --url "https://api.baseten.co/v1/models/<MODEL_ID>/environments/production" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $BASETEN_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "promotion_settings": {
      "rolling_deploy": true,
      "rolling_deploy_config": {
        "max_surge_percent": 25,
        "max_unavailable_percent": 10
      }
    }
  }'
```

results.title: Introducing Baseten Router: a Pareto-optimal model router for coding tasks
results.author: Guillaume Troadec, Matthew Blau, Aidan Phillips, Josh Green, Ervin Wang
highlights:
Baseten Router picks the right model per coding task, within 0.8 pts of Opus 5.5’s pass rate at 72% lower cost. Now in public preview on Baseten Grid.

...

Last updated

November 5, 2026

Originally published

November 4, 2026

TLDR

Baseten Router sends each coding task to the right model, open or closed, so you pay frontier prices only when the task needs it. In benchmarks, it came within 0.8 percentage points of Opus 5.5 at 72% lower cost. It’s the only router we tested that beat random routing by a statistically significant margin. Baseten Router is part of Baseten Grid, now in public preview.

Today, we’re sharing our initial results from training an intelligent model router for Baseten Grid.

Not every coding task needs the most capable model. As AI coding spend continues to grow rapidly [1] and cheaper open-weight models close the capability gap [2], choosing the right model for each task becomes increasingly valuable. Baseten Router chooses between models based on their expected performance and cost for each coding task. The goal is frontier performance while paying frontier prices only when the task calls for it.

Baseten Router cuts costs by 72% compared to using Opus 5.5 for every task while remaining within 0.8 percentage points of its pass rate, measured on a test set spanning DeepSWE, SWE Atlas QnA, and Terminal-Bench. Adjusting the routing threshold lets users choose various trade-offs along the cost-performance Pareto frontier.
